about.title: Saratoga Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a family in Saratoga loses a loved one because of someone else's negligence, the grief is immediate but the legal questions often aren't. California law gives close family members, and in some cases dependents, a path to hold the responsible party accountable through a civil wrongful death claim. This is separate from any criminal charges that might follow a fatal collision. Saratoga's local roads, including Saratoga Sunnyvale Road and Saratoga Los Gatos Road, see regular injury collisions each year, and while recent counts here show no traffic deaths in the latest final reporting year, fatal outcomes still happen on nearby freeways and surface streets. If your family is facing this loss, our team understands the toll this takes and can help you understand funeral costs, lost financial support, and other losses the law recognizes. There's no fee unless there's a recovery, and no obligation to move forward until you're ready.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Saratoga Choose Us

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to certain people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and then extending to other dependents or heirs. We can help clarify where your family stands before deadlines close in.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Window
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity can require action much sooner. Acting early preserves evidence and options while memories and records are still fresh.

items.title: Recognizing the Full Scope of Loss
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a loved one provided. We can help make sure these losses aren't overlooked in the process.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Saratoga?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death to file a civil wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as a public road authority, may be responsible, the deadline to act can be much shorter. Speaking with us early helps protect your family's options.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children typically have the first right to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible. We can review your family's situation and explain where you fit.

items.question: Saratoga's crash data shows no traffic deaths in the most recent year, so why would we need this service?
items.answer: That's true for the most recent final reporting year, but Santa Clara County as a whole, and nearby corridors like SR-85, still see fatal collisions in other years and surrounding areas. If your family has lost someone in a crash connected to Saratoga roads or elsewhere, we can still help you understand your legal options regardless of local statistics.
